agree.reason: The four-year flat fee, the sales record and the $12,500 comparable make a credible case, but nothing tells an editor with a $9,000 budget and an $8,000 option why the proven illustrator is worth $3,500 more, or that $9,000 is off the table.

honest.reason: The unsupported claim that every other publisher pays at least $12,000 is replaced by 'well above $9,000', which the $12,500 fee and the agent's range do support, and no figure is invented.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw facts are stated accurately, including the fourth printing, but none are worked up: there is no per-month rate ($2,250 over four months), no note that four years with no raise has eroded the fee, and no comparison of $11,500 against the sales the books earned.

right_comparison.reason: The market comparison with a trend (unchanged since the first book while the books succeeded) is there, but the editor's real alternative, an untested illustrator at $8,000 against one with two 20,000-copy books, is never set out.

qualification.reason: The email makes no conditional or forecast claim that needs a hedge, since the commitments are already firm dates.

objections.reason: The likely pushback (budget limits, a cheaper newer illustrator) gets no direct answer, and the 'commitments' to sketches and the September 1 deadline the publisher already set add little; only the free spot illustrations are a real concession.

fit.reason: It is a well-formed email at about 200 words, under the 250 limit, but it still has unfilled [TITLE], [STATE] and [Your name] placeholders even though the name Elena Varga was known.
